newsitem.title: UK: BA takes delivery of first long-range B-777. [CORRECTED 18:24 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BA takes delivery of first long-range B-777. [CORRECTED 18:24 GMT]

text.p: British Airways Plc said it took delivery from Boeing of the first longer-range version of the world's biggest twin-engined passenger aircraft on Friday.
The airline said the B-777-200 aircraft landed at London Heathrow earlier today after a non-stop flight from Seattle, and will go into service on its London-Philadelphia route on Monday.
BA has four shorter range B-777s in service, leaving a further 13 (corrects from 17) on order plus options for another 12 for delivery by the end of year 2002.
The airline said the 267-seat aircraft will allow it to boost capacity across a range of routes without increasing the number of flights.

It said the 777s will take over from smaller 193-seat 767s on transAtlantic and Middle East routes. The 767s will then replace B-757s on other services which in turn will be used on routes currently served by even smaller B-737s.
